original_target.title: A compact subset that cannot escape to infinity by homotopy
original_target.area: Riemannian geometry and topology of noncompact manifolds

full_original_statement:
Let $`(M,g)`$ be a smooth connected noncompact boundaryless complete Riemannian $`n`$-manifold, $`n\ge2`$, of finite volume. Assume that $`M`$ is **tame**: it is homeomorphic to the interior of a compact manifold with boundary. Retain both sectional-curvature bounds
```math
-b^2\le\mathrm{Sec}_g\le0
```

for some finite $`b>0`$.

Must there exist compact subsets $`C,K\subset M`$ such that every continuous map
```math
H:C\times[0,1]\longrightarrow M,\qquad H(c,0)=c,
```

satisfies
```math
H(C,1)\cap K\ne\varnothing?
```

Thus the inclusion of some compact $`C`$ cannot be homotoped outside every compact set. The endpoint need not be an embedding, and the homotopy is not required to be an ambient isotopy. No particular dimension or loop structure is required of $`C`$.

sources.scope_comparison: The exact target retains tameness, completeness, finite volume and both curvature bounds and asks exists compact C,K for all homotopies of the inclusion of C. The actual Conjecture9 states this compact-subset replacement. The primary source explicitly says its loop-only counterexamples do not refute it; its Sigma x R obstruction drops the uniform lower curvature bound. Pettet–Souto's maximal-flat result applies to locally symmetric manifolds, a special subclass. No general matching resolution or announcement was found by the bounded current searches.
